summary: PoC real-machine run for Issue #23 Phase C: enumerate devices and verify output path (sine) on Windows 11 / WASAPI / cpal 0.18.2

list_devices: 1 host (WASAPI). 5 output devices enumerated; default = "Analogue 1/2 (2- Audient iD4)". DeviceId is opaque 'wasapi:{...GUID...}'. All devices report Stereo-only F32 spaces: 16 discrete per-rate ranges (min==max per rate, 8000..384000 Hz, buffer_size fixed = rate/100) — WASAPI does not expose contiguous rate/buffer ranges

play_sine: default_output_format returned F32 44100Hz Stereo directly (no fallback needed). open_output_stream with BufferSize::Fixed(480) rejected with UnsupportedConfig; retry with BufferSize::Default succeeded. stream.buffer_size() reports Fixed(441) — the device period (10ms @44100) is reported post-open even though the request was Default

Output path verified: start() -> 496 data callbacks over ~5s -> stop(). Per-callback frame counts varied: min=88, max=441 (mean ~10ms period). Variable-frame delivery confirmed — bounded chunked write path exercised in production. error events: 0 (xrun=0). playback timestamp present on every callback (none_count=0); playback-callback delta ~32ms consistent with WASAPI latency

Timestamp anomaly: first callback timestamp recorded 0 ns while stream.now() and subsequent callback timestamps sit on the WASAPI device-clock scale (~5.046e13 ns). Suggests first-callback StreamInstant query returned epoch-0 or the adapter fallback path anchored at first callback — flagged for follow-up; not blocking (subsequent timestamps coherent, monotonic)

Callback-path allocation observed via counting #[global_allocator] (process-wide, includes cpal/WASAPI internals): 41 alloc events during open(); only 2 alloc + 2 dealloc events across the whole 5s streaming window (start->stop). Upper-bound measurement — cannot attribute to a thread; adapter self-code separately verified alloc-free via assert_no_alloc rt_ test (rt_output_callback_path_allocates_nothing)

Dependency rationale: cpal 0.18.2 as the evaluated backend (conditional-adoption candidate per ADR-034Jc9RslnH7QSQ1nZEEHL); assert_no_alloc 1.1.2 as dev-dependency for rt_-lane allocation verification of the adapter's own callback path. Counting #[global_allocator] probe kept inside the play_sine example only (local #[expect(unsafe_code)] + SAFETY comments)

Discovery Open Questions coverage: (1) callback alloc/blocking — observed: 2 process-wide alloc events during streaming; no blocking observed in adapter path. (2) BufferSize::Fixed fidelity — observed: Fixed(480) request rejected (UnsupportedConfig), device reports its own period Fixed(441) under Default; per-callback frames still vary 88..441. (3) Send/Sync variance — partially observed: port requires Send, held on WASAPI; cross-backend variance unmeasured. (4) WASAPI exclusive/ASIO need — not evaluated (out of scope). (5) ALSA vs PipeWire — unobserved: Windows environment, Linux lane pending. (6) RtContext fit — port keeps OutputCallbackInfo container shape; engine-level wiring unverified. WASAPI output xrun reporting: 0 events observed — cannot distinguish 'not occurred' from 'not reported' (WASAPI does not report output xruns; documented limitation)

Commands run: cargo build -p ruviform-audio-device --examples OK; cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings OK; cargo fmt --check OK; cargo run --example list_devices OK (WASAPI dump captured); cargo run --example play_sine OK (RESULT: OK — callbacks observed, exit 0). mise run fmt-check/lint pass. Raw outputs preserved at tmp/issue-23/{list_devices,play_sine}.out.txt

Judgment: enumerate -> default config -> stream start -> callback delivery verified end-to-end on real hardware. ADR promotion criteria (c) output-path demonstration and (d) callback non-alloc are satisfied (c: play_sine run; d: assert_no_alloc rt_ test + 2-event process-wide upper bound). Handed to T4 for ADR confirmation: unobserved items = ALSA vs PipeWire (Linux), Send/Sync cross-backend variance, WASAPI exclusive/ASIO necessity, first-callback timestamp=0 anomaly, Fixed-buffer honoring policy

Correction re-run after review fix: play_sine FIRST_CALLBACK_NS gauge was broken (AtomicI64::new(i64::MIN) + fetch_min never updates; printer mapped sentinel to 0). The seq5 'first callback timestamp 0' was an instrumentation artifact, not a backend-delivered value. Fixed to store-once compare_exchange and re-ran on the same host: this run opened on default device 'Digital Audio (S/PDIF) (High Definition Audio Device)' (the previously-default Audient iD4 was not the default this run), Fixed(480) was accepted this time (device-dependent), 503 callbacks, frames 96..480, callback first=55178557244100 last=55183556179900 ns (first is consistent with stream.now() 55178555903400 — no anomaly), playback last=55183588263234 none_count=0, 0 error events, 1 alloc event during streaming (process-wide upper bound), RESULT: OK. Also corrects seq4: the multi-chunk write path did NOT fire on hardware (n <= frames_capacity every callback); bounded chunked writing is unit-tested only.
